---
title: "1 · Ranking under uncertainty"
---

Sampling error can move a unit to the top or bottom of a ranking, especially when its estimate is imprecise. The [simulated league](noisy-league.qmd) shows how often this happens. We then calculate the posterior probability of a direction for [two units](two-units.qmd) and for every pair in a [probability matrix](pairwise-matrix.qmd). The remaining examples compare ways to rank units, estimate how many statements a ranking gets wrong, and examine how Monte Carlo error affects those estimates. The pairwise probabilities enter the decision to assign [ordered grades](../grades/index.qmd).
